========================================================================
 conctune report -- task 'demo' on golden-host
========================================================================

MACHINE
  Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8650U CPU @ 1.90GHz
  4 physical / 8 logical cores, 15.4 GiB RAM
  governor powersave, turbo on
  ! scaling governor powersave -- frequency ramps with load, so low worker counts run at lower clock and speedup looks inflated; consider 'performance' for the sweep
  ! turbo boost is on -- single-worker runs boost higher than saturated runs, which understates speedup; randomised run order mitigates but does not remove this
  ! SMT is on (4 physical / 8 logical) -- expect the speedup curve to bend at N=4, not N=8

WORKLOAD
  work  T1   = 4.47s  (measured per-case service times)
  span  Tinf = 0.81s  (18.2% of all work in one case)
  average parallelism T1/Tinf = 5.5

MEASURED
     N    wall (s)   speedup  efficiency   spread   failed
  ----------------------------------------------------------
     1       3.860      1.00        100%     0.0%        -
     2       2.077      1.86         93%     0.0%        -
     4       1.334      2.89         72%     0.0%        -
     8       1.216      3.17         40%     0.0%        -

UNIVERSAL SCALABILITY LAW
  sigma (contention) = 0.0361   -> Amdahl ceiling 27.7x
  kappa (coherency)  = 0.02263
  N*                 = 6.5
  peak speedup       = 3.24x
  R^2                = 1.0000

CEILINGS ON USEFUL CONCURRENCY
  startup       N <=    4.3   sqrt(work / B), measured boot cost  <== BINDING
                worker boot B=0.241s against 4.5s of work
  parallelism   N <=    5.5   work / span  
                work=4.5s, span=0.8s (longest single case is 18.2% of all work)
  overhead      N <=    6.5   USL peak, sqrt((1-sigma)/kappa)  
                coherency kappa=0.02263, contention sigma=0.0361
  hardware      N <=    7.2   cpus * work / cpu_total  
                at N=8: 5.0s CPU for 4.5s of work (90% of burned cycles useful)

LOAD BALANCE  (observed vs a greedy LPT schedule of the same cases,
               stretched by CPU growth over N=1, plus one worker boot)
     N   observed   LPT+boot      bound     ratio
  ------------------------------------------------
     2       2.08       2.50       2.48      0.83
     4       1.33       1.56       1.36      0.86
     8       1.22       1.28       1.06      0.95   (saturated)
  rows past N=4 are marked saturated: the cores are full there, so a case no longer runs at the
  service time measured without contention and the comparison says nothing about scheduling.

  ! observed makespan is below the lower bound for these cases, which is impossible -- the service times are overstated.
    Add [cases].startup to the task spec (or ignore this table); scheduling cannot be judged from it as it stands.

========================================================================
 RECOMMENDED WORKER COUNT: 8
   cheapest N within 3% of the best measured wall
========================================================================
   fastest measured : N=8 at 1.216s (3.17x over serial)
   knee of the curve: N=4
   binding constraint: startup (estimates N <= 4.3)
   ! the fastest point is the largest swept (N=8); the peak may lie beyond it -- extend --points and re-run
   ! the startup ceiling estimates N<=4.3, below the measured optimum of 8 -- the ceiling is a first-order estimate and the workers past it still win, just sub-linearly

STARTUP-BOUND -- measured worker boot cost B dominates: past sqrt(work/B) workers, booting them costs more than they save.
  - pool and reuse workers instead of booting one per batch
  - move imports, model loads and connection setup out of the per-worker path
  - batch small cases so each boot amortises over more work
  - fork from a warm parent instead of spawning a cold interpreter
